reports.title: Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Interim Financial Statements(In US dollars) HUDBAY MINERALS INC. For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025

lines: • Further improved full year 2026 consolidated cash cost1 guidance range to $(0.55) to $(0.35) per pound of copper, an additional improvement from the previously updated guidance range of $(0.45) to $(0.25) per pound of copper, as year-to-date results are trending well below the low end of the cash cost range.

• Improved full year 2026 consolidated sustaining cash cost guidance range to $1.40 to $1.80 per pound copper from the original guidance range of $1.70 to $2.10 per pound of copper as a result of strong exposure to gold by-product credits and continued strong operating cost control.

Full year 2026 consolidated sustaining capital expenditures expected to be $35 million lower than guidance levels due to lower capitalized stripping in Peru and British Columbia and capital deferrals and efficiencies.

Peru cash cost1, net of by-product credits, of $2.23 per pound exceeded the upper end of the 2026 annual guidance range of $1.70 to $2.10 per pound primarily due to lower by-product credits, partially offset by better treatment and refining charges.
Manitoba cash cost1 of $403 per ounce of gold outperformed the low end of the 2026 annual guidance range of $500 to $800 per ounce as a result of higher by-product prices.

With the successful execution of its disciplined capital allocation strategy, attracting Mitsubishi as a long-term strategic joint venture partner and a prudent project funding plan, Hudbay's Copper World capital contributions are expected to be approximately $500 million, representing less than 25% of the initial growth capital, with capital contributions not expected to be required until 2028.
